title: SDK Bridge Patterns & Back-compat Examples for v1->v2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a set of concrete "bridge" patterns and example adapters that help teams migrate from v1 SDK ergonomics to v2 without breaking production. Deliver docs, language-specific code examples (Python/TypeScript/Go), and a small compatibility helper package that provides optional shims. Also add changelog automation hooks to surface deprecations and compatibility notes per release.
background: v2 of Redwood SDK introduces an async-first streaming API, a new retry/middleware abstraction, and renamed configuration fields. Several customers and internal teams reported difficulty porting large codebases that rely on v1 streaming callbacks, synchronous wrappers, and custom retry logic. We need documented patterns and small helper adapters that reduce migration risk while encouraging idiomatic v2 usage.
proposed_solution: Deliver three components: (1) "bridge" adapter implementations (python package redwood_sdk_compat/adapter.py, ts package @redwood/compat, go package redwood/compat) that translate v1 callback/iterator patterns to v2 async iterators and vice versa; (2) a migration guide with per-language recipes and minimal-change code snippets; (3) CI-based changelog automation that extracts deprecation metadata from SDK code to generate human-friendly notes. Avoid shipping these shims as default imports; make them opt-in and clearly marked as temporary.

acceptance_criteria: A1: Adapter packages exist in monorepo and can be imported opt-in (python: redwood_sdk_compat; ts: @redwood/compat; go: redwood/compat)
A2: Migration guide contains at least one end-to-end example per language that converts a v1 streaming callback pattern to v2 async iterator, with retry behavior preserved
A3: Changelog automation adds a 'compatibility' section to release notes when deprecations or opt-in shims are present
A4: Tests demonstrating parity for retries (exponential backoff and jitter), including idempotency guidance for common generator examples
A5: Docs reviewed by SDK and Developer Experience leads and published on docs.redwood.dev
risks: R1: Shims may encourage long-term reliance on non-idiomatic APIs — mitigate by marking as deprecated and adding telemetry to measure usage
R2: Subtle semantic differences in streaming (ordering, partial failures) could cause regressions — mitigate with e2e tests and example harnesses
R3: Changelog automation may miss manually-crafted deprecation reasons — include a review step in the release checklist
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting — agreed to keep adapters opt-in and short-lived. Assigned Python and TS work to Miguel and Go to Lin.

2026-02-16: Prototype for python adapter complete. Uses an async generator wrapper that yields v2 token events and translates v1 callback signatures. Edge case: early abort needs to drain KV cache correctly — added note in design doc.
2026-02-24: TypeScript adapter wrapped as AsyncIterable with AbortSignal support. Added test simulating network hiccup to verify retry middleware replays safely where idempotent.

reviewers_feedback: DevEx (Leah Kim): 'Adapters look helpful. Please make examples small and copy-pasteable; avoid heavy framework dependencies.'
SDK (Rajesh Kumar): 'Ensure retry middleware remains orthogonal — adapters must not change retry semantics by default. Document best-practices for idempotency checks.'
Security (Olivia Martinez): 'Changelog action will run in CI; ensure tokens are read from repo secrets and action does not expose deprecation metadata publicly by accident.'
implementation_notes: Python adapter pattern: provide sync wrapper -> wraps v2 async iterator using asyncio.to_thread for minimal changes, and an explicit 'compat.retry' decorator to emulate v1 behavior.
TS adapter pattern: export makeV1StreamFromV2(v2Client) -> returns (onData, onEnd, onError) registration function for existing callers. Also export promisified resumeToken helpers.
Go adapter pattern: StreamAdapter struct implements v1 Stream interface by spawning a goroutine that reads from v2 stream channel and forwards events; uses context cancellation to close cleanly.

Changelog automation: use code annotations like @deprecated(since="2.0.0", reason="Use client.streamV2()") and a small parser that emits JSON used by GitHub Action. Action generates docs/md fragment and attaches to release draft.
Telemetry: add optional flag to adapters to emit a single usage ping (configurable) to measure migration velocity. Keep ping off by default for enterprise privacy-sensitive installs.
